end.summary:
• Practised making one mark for each object to keep track.
• Matched marks back to objects to check for missing or extra items.
• Used examples with goats, cows, plates, boats, stones, and bangles.
• Repeatedly linked one large object with two marks and spread-out rows with more objects.
• Did not yet explain why one-to-one matching works without number names.
end.parentNote: Parth practised pairing one mark with each object and checking whether every object had a match. They suggested using one stone for each boat, showing the tracking method in that example. They mixed up object size with the number of marks and continued to think a spread-out row had more bangles; this was not corrected by the end. At home, place small objects in two rows, spread one row out, and have Parth match each object one-to-one without counting aloud.

बराबर ही तो हैं? पर... नहीं, फैलाने से चूड़ियाँ ज़्यादा लग रही हैं। चूड़ियाँ ही ज़्यादा हैं।

Tumhe choodiyan zyada lag rahi hain, kyunki line lambi dikhti hai. Chalo, har bindi aur uski choodi ko ek dori se jodo. Choodi sarakne par dori lambi hogi, jodi nahi badlegi. Kya har bindi ko ab bhi apni choodi milti hai?
हर बिंदी को अपनी चूड़ी तो मिल रही है... पर अब लाइन बड़ी है, तो चूड़ियाँ ज़्यादा ही हैं।
Har bindi ko apni choodi mil rahi hai. Tumhe lambi line dekhkar choodiyan zyada lag rahi hain. Socho, agar phaili line se ek choodi hata dein, toh uski bindi ko choodi milegi?
